2608.21206.title: No PUN Intended: Plausible Unknown Names for Person-Centred LLM Evaluation
2608.21206.paper_summary: Person names are widely used as prompt variables in LLM evaluations of factuality, privacy leakage, bias and abstention, but when a name's evidential status is uncontrolled, measurements may conflate memorisation, retrieval, name priors and wrong-person attribution. We operationalise an unknown name as one with plausible First-Last form, no indexed full-name evidence, and no ambiguity signals under a documented validation run, and introduce PUN (Plausible Unknown Names), a protocol for constructing and validating such names, combining Wikidata-derived components, web-enabled LLM screening, and controlled search revalidation. We report acceptance rate, reproducibility, ablations, and a 204-participant human study, finding accepted names are more name-like than controls while participants recover person evidence in only 3% of cases. We release 300 names with comparison controls.
2608.21206.paper_summary_zh: 人名在大型語言模型（LLM）對事實性、隱私洩漏、偏見和放棄的評估中被廣泛用作提示變數，但當一個名字的證據狀態無法控制時，測量可能會混淆記憶、檢索、名字先驗和錯誤人員歸屬。我們將未知名字操作化為具有合理的名-姓形式、沒有索引的全名證據，以及在記錄的驗證運行中沒有歧義信號的名字，並引入PUN（合理未知名字），這是一種構建和驗證此類名字的協議，結合了來自Wikidata的組件、網絡啟用的LLM篩選和受控搜索再驗證。我們報告了接受率、可重複性、消融實驗和一項包含204名參與者的人類研究，發現被接受的名字比對照組更像名字，而參與者在僅3%的情況下恢復了人員證據。我們發布了300個名字及其比較對照。
2608.21206.author: Dimitri Staufer et.al.
